content: Menyanthes is a genus of flowering plants that contains only one species, classified under the family Menyanthaceae. The name Menyanthes is derived from the Greek words menyein, meaning disclosing, and anthos, meaning flower. This name refers to the sequential opening of flowers along the plant's inflorescence. The species Menyanthes trifoliata is distinguished by its horizontal rhizome and alternate, trifoliate leaves. Its inflorescence is an upright raceme composed of white flowers. This plant is typically found in bogs and marshes across Asia, Europe, and North America. In North America, a specific form of this species is often referred to as Menyanthes trifoliata var. minor Michx. In English, Menyanthes trifoliata is commonly known as bog-bean or buckbean. In German, it is referred to as Bitterklee or Fieberklee.
